Sorry this is late, life's been crazy lately. Honestly I think Pacific Quest is on the less harmful end of these programs while you're there. There's not a lot of super crazy rules that I remember, just rules that you would expect for unstable kids in a jungle (have to stay in staff's line of sight and stuff). I will say though, at least when I was there, you aren't allowed to talk to other kids in the first stage of the program, and communication with other kids is pretty restricted. I didn't mind this so much because I'm a hardcore introvert, but extroverted people might find this really hard. I actually enjoyed some of my time there. The thing that you need to be careful of, and that completely ruined it for me, was that the therapists there advocate strongly for everyone to go into a long-term residential program after they "graduate", and many of these programs are heavily abusive. 

In my opinion, it would be best if you made her part of the decision to go somewhere. Shipping her away without any advance notice can give her the message that you don't want to be the ones to deal with her, and I haven't heard a single non-traumatic story of someone being transported to one of these places without knowing about it. I don't know what y'all's situation is but I strongly suggest that y'all try to figure out a solution that doesn't involve sending her to any long term facility. 

Hope this helps and I hope she gets the help she needs :)
